receipt.head: e975cd684b48d9f1cc38c865f7b6b4cbb13c1e0c
receipt.authority: User requested local independent review; permanent global review execution exception retained.

findings.impact: The split hashes section-specific row IDs independently, allowing identical servings into dev and holdout. Yoshinoya's 290 g Japanese Udon Noodles appears in bulk.dev.jsonl:99 and bulk.holdout.jsonl:78 with identical macros; the 113 g Mixed Veggies repeats this at lines 101 and 79. This violates the accepted serving-grouped holdout contract and compromises later generalization measurements. Impact is bounded to the offline evaluation, but the population needs correction before baseline tuning.
findings.summary: Group equivalent published servings before assigning splits.
findings.scenario: The same Yoshinoya component is published under Regular Combo and Combo XL headings -> different IDs place its identical serving and labels in both splits.
findings.fix: Define reviewed serving-equivalence groups and assign one split per group while retaining contextual row IDs. Reuse that identity throughout build.ts split assignment, candidate filtering and case grouping; version and review affected frozen artifacts. Do not equate unrelated dishes merely because their macro vectors match.

findings.impact: The modifier generator interprets 'Bowls' anywhere in the section as evidence that the reference contains rice. curated:match:094 consequently expects NO MATCH for a 250 g chicken-only component with 'no rice', while offering that unchanged component as a candidate. sources/curation.json:471 explicitly identifies this row as a component, and its false negative is visible in docs/engineering/pipeline/eval-suite-cases.md:115. This corrupts one curated label and rewards rejecting a valid serving; the effect is bounded and repairable.
findings.summary: Choose modifier challenges from the actual recipe rather than section-name keywords.
findings.scenario: Grilled Teriyaki Chicken under 'Combo XL Bowls / Select Two Large Proteins' receives 'no rice' -> removing an absent ingredient is labeled as a changed recipe requiring NO MATCH.
findings.fix: Specify the concrete modifier in sources/curation.json, following its explicit scenario-plan approach, and use a modification that actually changes this component or select a rice-containing meal. Remove the section-keyword inference and review the regenerated label.

findings.impact: A transient append or fsync failure after a provider response leaves the reservation unsettled because accounting and stop-state updates occur after both journal writes. run.ts:43 swallows the exception as an adapter failure, and run.ts:96 permits subsequent requests because stopped remains null. Restarting detects the pending reservation, but the current collector continues with understated spend, violating the durable-reservation stop contract. This is an uncommon, recoverable collection failure rather than production payment harm.
findings.summary: Stop collection when any request-journaling operation fails.
findings.scenario: A billed response arrives, then its exchange append or settlement fsync throws a transient I/O error while later writes succeed -> the runner sends more requests despite an unsettled reservation and records no cost for the failed item.
findings.fix: Latch stopped and unresolved accounting on any exceptional exit after reservation, preventing further sends until reconciliation. Preserve pending receipts and propagate journal failures as collector failures. Follow the abort-on-journal-write-error boundary in scripts/eval/lib/jev-experiment.ts:205 and cover response and settlement write failures.
